rubric.why: Identifies the name of the chemical formula being defined.
rubric.description: Names it as the molecular formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the formula as a molecular formula.

rubric.why: States what information the molecular formula shows.
rubric.description: Says it shows the types of atoms bonded together in one molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it shows the atoms bonded together in a molecule.

modelAnswer: A chemical compound is thus, represented by a chemical formula which is called the molecular formula of that compound and which shows all the types of atoms bonded together in one molecule of that compound.

rubric.why: Gives the defining ratio and its simplest form.
rubric.description: States that the ratio is the simplest whole number ratio.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a simplest whole-number ratio.

rubric.why: Specifies what the ratio refers to.
rubric.description: Says the ratio is of atoms present in the compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the ratio concerns atoms in the compound.

modelAnswer: Empirical Formula of a compound shows the simplest whole number ratio of atoms present in that compound.

rubric.why: States what Avogadro's number counts and the amount it applies to.
rubric.description: Identifies it as the number of units or particles in one mole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the number of units or particles in one mole.

rubric.why: Gives the symbol used for Avogadro's number.
rubric.description: States that it is represented as Nₐ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving Nₐ as its representation.

modelAnswer: Avogadro's number is the number of units in one mole of a substance. This number is represented as Nₐ.

rubric.why: States the defining quantity of particles.
rubric.description: Says the substance contains Avogadro's number of particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Avogadro's number of particles.

rubric.why: Identifies the quantity as a mole.
rubric.description: States that this quantity of substance is called a mole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the quantity of substance as a mole.

modelAnswer: The quantity of a substance containing Avogadro's number of particles (Nₐ) is called a Mole.

rubric.why: States the amount of substance whose mass is being defined.
rubric.description: Identifies the mass as that of one mole of a substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the mass is for one mole.

rubric.why: Gives the name of this quantity.
rubric.description: Names the mass of one mole as molar mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as molar mass.

modelAnswer: The mass of one mole of a substance is called Molar mass.

rubric.description: States that a chemical change is represented.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the representation of a chemical change.

rubric.why: Gives the name of this representation.
rubric.description: Identifies it as a chemical equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the representation as a chemical equation.

modelAnswer: Representing a chemical change in this way is called a chemical equation.
